title: On‑Prem Deployment Assessment — Field Interview Notes (Customer: Atlas Financial)
content:
Purpose:
Notes from on-site field interview with Atlas Financial (initial POC scoping, security and network constraints for an air-gapped private deployment). Goal: capture environment inventory, non-functional constraints, suggested deployment approaches, risks, and immediate next steps for a 6–8 week POC.

Meeting metadata:
- Date: 2025-08-08
- Location: Atlas HQ (Boston) / Hybrid
- Attendees (customer): Priya Menon (Cloud Infra Lead), Tom Baylor (Security Architect), Jenna Ruiz (Data Privacy), Martin Cho (Platform Ops)
- Redwood attendees: Evelyn Chen (SE, lead), Miguel Torres (infra), Asha Patel (security SME)

Executive summary (one paragraph):
Atlas requires a private, air-gapped deployment of Redwood for inference of internal customer-support assistants and document embedding. Primary constraints are strict egress prohibition from the inference subnet, FIPS-compatible crypto requirements, and an internal demand for signed images and attestable upgrade procedures. They prefer a semi-manual bootstrap path (sneakernet or ephemeral bastion) and have modest capacity needs initially (2–4 GPUs, throughput spikes for batch re-indexing). Recommend staged POC: (1) architect & security review, (2) air-gap bootstrap dry-run in Atlas staging, (3) single-cluster pilot with synthetic traffic, (4) limited production roll.

Environment inventory (captured):
- Hardware: 2 x DGX-style nodes (A100 class) in primary datacenter, expansion rack in DR room (spare GPUs available).
- Orchestration: Kubernetes 1.27 managed by platform team (kubeadm on locked-down nodes). No upstream cluster access for third parties.
- Storage: NFS provisioner for model artifacts (100TB headroom), Ceph available for object store (RGW) but with offline replication windows.
- Network: Strict internal firewall rules, egress explicitly blocked from inference subnets. No NAT egress except via an approved jump host. VLAN segmentation enforced.
- Identity: Internal OIDC provider (Keycloak) + Active Directory for service accounts; RBAC must map to AD groups.
- Secrets & keys: HSM available via vendor (Thales). Customer expects KMS integration and keywrap support for model keys.

Hard constraints & non-negotiables:
- Absolutely no outbound internet from inference nodes (air-gap).
- All binaries and container images must be signed and verifiable offline (they requested experience with Sigstore but can accept vendor signing).
- Cryptography must be FIPS-approved in applicable data flows.
- Audit logs must be stored for 1 year in immutable store; platform must support tamper-evident logging.
- PII cannot leave the Atlas network; any telemetry must be opt-in and stored on-prem.

Customer preferences (soft constraints):
- Prefer an operator-run install rather than fully automated SaaS-style bootstrap.
- Would like a documented rollback plan and clear playbook (checklists) for upgrades.
- Observability via internal ELK stack is preferred over external SaaS.

Deployment options considered (notes):
1) Air-gapped installer bundle (recommended for POC):
   - Deliver tarball with pre-signed container images, binaries, CRDs, Helm manifests, and a signature file.
   - Atlas to transfer bundle via approved media; Redwood guides offline verification and install steps.
   - Advantage: minimal blast radius, no outbound required; easier for security review.
   - Effort: ~3–4 engineer-weeks to prepare hardened bundle + offline verification scripts.

2) Bastion-assisted bootstrap (semi-automated):
   - Use ephemeral bastion host with controlled internet to pull images, then push into internal registry.
   - Requires strict ephemeral access policy and audited session recording.
   - Advantage: faster iteration; disadvantage: introduces an egress window that security may disallow.

3) Full airgap appliance (long-term):
   - Turnkey appliance (VMs) shipped to Atlas running preinstalled runtime. More ops burden to maintain.
   - Advantage: minimizes on-site operator work; disadvantage: appliance maintenance lifecycle.

Security & compliance specifics:
- Image signing: customer expects image provenance verification step; propose using cosign offline signing and documenting public key distribution process.
- KMS/HSM: integrate Redwood key encryption layer with Thales HSM via PKCS#11 adapter; require keywrap and rotation process in playbook.
- Attestation: hardware/software attestation desirable (TPM measured boot). Discussed using simple signed manifests initially, then exploring more formal attestation later.
- Network: need documented firewall rules and required ports. Customer will provision a dedicated VLAN with strict ACLs; we must minimize required port openings.
- Audit: propose forwarding logs to central ELK over internal secure channel; provide local buffered fallback in case of ELK outage.

Operational considerations (obs/logging/metrics):
- Metrics pipeline: Prometheus metrics scraped within VLAN; recommend Prometheus remote-write to internal TSDB.
- Traces: Jaeger on-prem or light-weight agent; privacy filter applied before retention.
- Logs: Fluentd/Vector to ELK with TLS and mutual auth. Telemetry that leaves cluster must be configurable and off by default.

Upgrade & rollback strategy (POC scope):
- Rolling upgrade with canary on a single replica; preflight health checks (kv-cache warm, model warmup duration).
- Offline patching workflow for security fixes: produce signed patch bundle, test in staging offline cluster, apply per node with documented fallback to snapshot-based rollback.

Backup & disaster recovery:
- Model artifacts replicated to Ceph RGW snapshots weekly; recommend nightly incremental and weekly full snapshot stored offsite on tape/immutable store.
- KV cache ephemeral; only model artifacts and critical configuration need durable backup.

Estimated POC timeline and effort (high level):
- Week 0: Kickoff, access & logistics, security questionnaire (1 week)
- Week 1–2: Package air-gap installer, prepare signed images, create playbook and runbooks (2 weeks)
- Week 3: Customer performs offline transfer and install with Redwood on-call (1 week)
- Week 4: Synthetic validation tests, load profile, perf baselining (1 week)
- Week 5–6: Adjustments, security review sign-off, handoff to Atlas ops (2 weeks)
Estimated Redwood effort: ~5–8 engineer-weeks (split across SE, security SME, infra eng).

Risk register (top items):
- Risk: Image verification mismatch or key distribution failure.
  Severity: High.
  Mitigation: Pre-test signing/verification with customer KMS before on-site; provide fallback manual fingerprint checks.
- Risk: Network ACLs block required service ports.
  Severity: Medium.
  Mitigation: Provide minimal port matrix and test harness to validate firewall rules ahead of transfer.
- Risk: HSM integration delays (vendor SDK/config quirks).
  Severity: Medium-High.
  Mitigation: Early engagement with Thales team; mock HSM in staging for dev testing.
- Risk: Audit retention requirements not met by initial POC.
  Severity: Medium.
  Mitigation: Implement temporary long-term storage for logs until full integration.

Open questions (items requiring Atlas input):
- Which AD groups map to Redwood service roles? (asked: Priya to supply list)
- Can the platform team accept a temporary bastion for image ingestion if sessions are strictly recorded? (Tom to confirm)
- Exact retention window for telemetry and whether any telemetry can be forwarded off-net with prior approval.
- Do they require FIPS-mode across the entire OS stack or only for key-management and TLS? (Jenna to clarify)

Immediate next steps / action items:
- Redwood (Evelyn/Miguel): produce draft air-gap bundle and offline verification script by 2025-08-20.
- Atlas (Priya): provide AD group mappings and internal pull request for firewall exceptions (if any) by 2025-08-18.
- Redwood security (Asha): run a quick HSM compatibility checklist and list known PKCS#11 caveats (due 2025-08-19).
- Schedule follow-up technical workshop (3 hours) to walk through playbook and offline install flow (target week of 2025-08-25).

Appendix — quick checklist for field engineers (compact):
- Bring: signed bundle checksum (sha256), cosign public key file, install playbook, offline verification script, USB with signed images.
- Validate: cluster kubelet versions, available volume plugin for NFS/Ceph, available kernel modules for GPU drivers, TPM presence (if attestation planned).
- Ports to request: (minimal set) etcd (internal cluster), kubelet, node-exporter, Redis (if used), and 1 outbound to internal ELK for log sink (TLS). Provide final matrix in separate doc.

Raw customer quotes (verbatim capture):
- "We cannot have anything call home without a signed and auditable change request." — Tom (Security Architect)
- "If you can get us a reproducible offline install, we'll be willing to run it in staging ASAP." — Priya (Infra Lead)

Notes on differences vs standard hosted POC: offline image lifecycle and tight HSM/KMS coupling are the main additional efforts. Lower iteration velocity is expected.

Prepared by: Evelyn Chen (SE) — contact: evelyn.chen@redwood.example
